# I-1 · Control Implementation

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Step | I Implement (system level) |
| Phases | PH-EMD (primary) |
| Depends on | S-6 |
| Inputs | ART-SSP, ART-BIA, EXT-STIG, EXT-PRODUCT |
| Outputs | ART-STIG (produces) |
| Writes facts | — |
| Minimum interviews | 1 |
| RACI | R: PER-PM, PER-CCP, PER-DEV, PER-ISSE · A: PER-PM · C: PER-IO, PER-PRIV, PER-ISSM, PER-ISSO, PER-LSE · I: — · PER-PRIV only when the system processes PII |
| Persona cards | [PER-PM](../../personas/PER-PM.md), [PER-CCP](../../personas/PER-CCP.md), [PER-DEV](../../personas/PER-DEV.md), [PER-ISSE](../../personas/PER-ISSE.md), [PER-IO](../../personas/PER-IO.md), [PER-PRIV](../../personas/PER-PRIV.md), [PER-ISSM](../../personas/PER-ISSM.md), [PER-ISSO](../../personas/PER-ISSO.md), [PER-LSE](../../personas/PER-LSE.md) |

Purpose: Implement the controls in the approved security plan through systems security engineering, applying STIG/SRG secure configurations, and design them into the product baseline by the CDR.
<!-- END rmf:header -->
<!-- rmf:body authored -->

## Steps

1. **Entry check.** S-6 is done: ART-SSP records the AO's (or AODR's) approval of the
   security plan. Why: I-1 implements the controls of the **approved** plan; changes to the
   plan come back through I-2, not through I-1.
2. **Read the inputs** in `## Inputs`. From the SSP family files note the controls whose
   status is `planned` or `partial` (the implementation work) and every statement that
   names a configuration setting. From `artifacts/data/inventory.yaml` list the items of
   kind `software`, `operating-system`, `database`, `firmware`, `virtual-machine`,
   `hardware` and `network-device`: those need a secure configuration benchmark or a
   not-applicable rationale (STIG-001; DoDI 8500.01 holds all DoD IT to the STIGs and SRGs).
3. **Understand what the agent does here.** In a run, implementation is the program's
   engineering work; the agent does not build anything. I-1 records the
   secure-configuration (STIG/SRG) state of every inventory item, and captures in its
   interviews how the controls were implemented, as the developer and engineers report it
   and the product material shows it. Why: SP 800-37r2 Task I-1 expects implemented
   controls; I-2 turns those answers into the as-implemented SSP, and A-2 and A-3 use the
   STIG results as evidence.
4. **Interview** PER-DEV (what was built and configured, scan results), PER-ISSE (how the
   engineering methods and the architecture were followed, deviations from the plan) and
   PER-CCP (how the inherited controls were put in place for this system). Ask for
   evidence: configuration baselines, scan dates, benchmark versions, open findings.
5. **Map benchmarks.** For each inventory item of those kinds,
   find the applicable DISA STIG or SRG (EXT-STIG; DoDI 8510.01 requires their use, see
   `## Citations`), and where none applies the NSA/CSS security implementation and
   mitigation guidance, a DoD security configuration guide, a NIST checklist or mitigation
   guideline, or the vendor's hardening guidance (DoDI 8531.01):
   - a benchmark record: `id` (`BM-01`, ...), `title`, `version`, `kind` (`stig`, `srg`,
     `nsa-guide`, `security-configuration-guide`, `nist-checklist`, `vendor-guide`),
     `applies_to` (the `INV-###` items), `scan_date` when a scan ran;
   - an item with no applicable STIG or SRG goes in `not_applicable` with a rationale
     (for example firmware without an IP stack, protected by signed images);
   - a finding record per open or reviewed rule the scan reported: `id` (`STG-###`,
     numbered across the run), `benchmark`, `rule_id` (`V-`/`SV-`), `category`
     (`CAT I`/`CAT II`/`CAT III`), `inventory_item`, `title`, `status` (`open`,
     `not-a-finding`, `not-applicable`, `not-reviewed`, `exception`), and `control_id` when
     the rule maps to a control. A deviation the system keeps is `status: exception` with an
     `exception` record: its rationale, `approved_by` (PER-AO, or PER-AODR on the AO's
     behalf) and the date (DoDI 8500.01, SCFG-001). A deviation not yet approved stays
     `open` and goes through configuration management.
   Use only benchmark titles and results the product material or the answers give; a
   benchmark the answers cannot confirm is an assumption (`_shared/tagging-and-traceability.md`).
   Why: STIG-001 fails on an item of those kinds without a mapping or a not-applicable
   rationale, and STIG-002 later fails on an open CAT I finding without a POA&M item.
6. **Write `artifacts/data/stig-summary.yaml`** whole (schema
   `framework/schema/stig-summary.schema.json`), with the file-level `sources` naming the
   scan results:

   ```yaml
   benchmarks:
     - id: BM-01
       title: "General Purpose Operating System SRG"
       version: "V3R1"
       kind: srg
       applies_to: [INV-002]
       scan_date: "2026-09-30"
   not_applicable:
     - inventory_item: INV-006
       rationale: "Radio firmware has no applicable STIG or SRG; images are signed."
   findings:
     - id: STG-001
       benchmark: BM-01
       rule_id: SV-900101
       category: CAT II
       inventory_item: INV-002
       title: "Security updates are not installed within the defined period"
       status: open
       control_id: si-2
   sources: [product/test-results.md#config-scan, INT-021.A2]
   ```

7. **Write `artifacts/ART-STIG.md`** from `templates/artifacts/ART-STIG.md`, filling its
   sections, each traced:
   - `## Applicability`: the benchmarks per inventory item (`BM-##`, `INV-###`) and the
     not-applicable decisions with their reason;
   - `## Scan results`: scan dates and the tool named as in `tools` of `artifacts/data/cm-plan.yaml`,
     finding counts by category and status;
   - `## Open findings`: the open findings, CAT I first, by `STG-###` with the related
     control and the planned fix;
   - `## Accepted deviations`: deviations from a benchmark approved through configuration
     management, with the approval, or a sentence saying none.
   Name records by ID; the YAML is their one home. Keep the template's comment about A-3's
   `## Assessor verification` section; A-3 appends it.
8. **Leave the SSP alone.** Do not change `artifacts/ssp/controls/*.yaml` or ART-SSP even
   when an answer shows the implementation differs from the plan. Journal a NOTE naming the
   controls and the answers instead; I-2 updates the plan to the as-implemented state and
   reads them. Why: I-1's only output is ART-STIG; I-2 owns the SSP update.
9. **Build and check.** `uv run rmf build <run>`, then `uv run rmf check <run> --task I-1`,
   until 0 errors.
10. **Journal** a CHECKPOINT.

## Interviews

| Persona | Why | Question focus |
|---|---|---|
| PER-DEV | responsible (R) | how each planned control was built or configured; STIG/SRG scans, versions, dates and open rules |
| PER-ISSE | responsible (R) | engineering methods used, architecture deviations, assurance for third-party components |
| PER-CCP | responsible (R) | how the inherited controls were put in place for this system |
| PER-ISSO (optional) | consulted (C) | operational settings (accounts, logging) and who keeps them |
| PER-PM (optional) | accountable (A) | implementation decisions that changed the plan, and their approval |

At least 1 interview; this playbook expects PER-DEV and PER-ISSE interviews.

## Inputs

- `artifacts/ART-SSP.md`, `artifacts/ssp/controls/<fam>.yaml` (the approved plan)
- `artifacts/data/inventory.yaml` (items to map to benchmarks)
- Product material (EXT-PRODUCT): configuration and scan results, for example
  `product/test-results.md`
- STIGs and SRGs (EXT-STIG): titles and versions as the product material or answers give
  them; the requirement to use them:
  `uv run rmf refs show DODI8510.01 --page 6 --anchor "security requirements guides, and security technical implementation guides"`

## Outputs

| File | Front-matter | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `artifacts/data/stig-summary.yaml` | — | schema `stig-summary`, written whole |
| `artifacts/ART-STIG.md` | `artifact_id: ART-STIG`, `produced_by_task: I-1`, `touched_by: [I-1]` | template `templates/artifacts/ART-STIG.md`; A-3 appends itself |

## Facts

I-1 writes no facts.

## Done when

- `stig-summary.yaml` maps every software, operating-system, database, firmware and
  virtual-machine inventory item to a benchmark or a not-applicable rationale (STIG-001),
  and lists the open findings.
- ART-STIG records the applicability, scan results, open findings and accepted deviations.
- `uv run rmf check <run> --task I-1` reports 0 errors.

## Journal and lessons

- CHECKPOINT: `## <time> · CHECKPOINT · task I-1`, with the benchmark count and the open
  findings per category.
- An open CAT I finding is worth a NOTE for A-6 (STIG-002 needs a POA&M item for it).
